newsitem.title: INDIA: Dozens feared drowned in India bus accident.
newsitem.headline: Dozens feared drowned in India bus accident.

text.p: About 40 people are believed to have died on Tuesday when a crowded bus was swept away while crossing a flooded river in eastern India, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.
The news agency said the accident occurred in the Giridih district of Bihar state while the bus was crossing the monsoon-swollen Usri river.
PTI quoted senior district official Sujata Chaturvedi as saying she feared about 40 people had been killed.
Witnesses at the scene said they believed 70 people could have died in the accident 200 km (125 miles) southeast of the Bihar state capital, Patna.
Chaturvedi was quoted as saying the bus might have been carried several miles (km) from the road crossing by strong currents.
The agency did not say have many people were believed to have been on board.
PTI quoted witnesses as saying the possibility of survivors appeared slim.
Monsoon rains, from June to September, cause havoc with normal life in India where a poor drainage system fails to cope with the excess water.

Last Thursday, 25 people died when a bus fell into a waterlogged ditch near Biharsharif in the same state. On Saturday, 27 people drowned when a bus fell into a swollen river in the neighbouring state of Uttar Pradesh.
